carnotaurus:eswiki:15.title: Carnotaurus sastrei (Cinética del cráneo y mordida)

facts.statement: Carnotaurus lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 69 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period, between 69 and 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Carnotaurus was discovered in 1984 in the Chubut Province of Argentina within the La Colonia Formation.
facts.quote: The skeleton, found in 1984, was uncovered in the Chubut Province of Argentina from rocks of the La Colonia Formation.

facts.statement: The only known skeleton of Carnotaurus was unearthed in 1984 by an expedition led by paleontologist José Bonaparte.
facts.quote: The only skeleton (holotype MACN-CH 894) was unearthed in 1984 by an expedition led by Argentinian paleontologist José Bonaparte.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte named the genus and species Carnotaurus sastrei in 1985 based on a brief description of the skull and lower jaw.
facts.quote: In 1985, Bonaparte published a note presenting Carnotaurus sastrei as a new genus and species and briefly describing the skull and lower jaw.

facts.statement: The name Carnotaurus translates to "meat-eating bull," referencing the animal's bull-like horns.
facts.quote: The generic name Carnotaurus is derived from the Latin carno [carnis] ("flesh") and taurus ("bull") and can be translated with "meat-eating bull", an allusion to the animal's bull-like horns.

facts.statement: The species name sastrei honors Angel Sastre, the ranch owner where the fossil was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name sastrei honors Angel Sastre, the owner of the ranch where the skeleton was found.

facts.statement: A comprehensive description of the entire Carnotaurus skeleton was published in 1990.
facts.quote: A comprehensive description of the whole skeleton followed in 1990.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus was a lightly built, bipedal predator that measured between 7.5 and 8 meters in length and weighed between 1.3 and 2.1 metric tons.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus was a lightly built, bipedal predator, measuring 7.5 to 8 m in length and weighing 1.3 - 2.1 MT.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus possessed two thick horns above its eyes, a feature unique among all known carnivorous dinosaurs, and a deep skull supported by a muscular neck.
facts.quote: It had two thick horns above the eyes, a unique feature unseen in all other carnivorous dinosaurs, and a very deep skull sitting on a muscular neck.

facts.statement: The skin pattern included large bumps lining the sides of the animal, and there is no evidence of feathers.
facts.quote: The mosaic was interrupted by large bumps that lined the sides of the animal, and there are no hints of feathers.

facts.statement: At 7.5 to 8 meters long, the known individual of Carnotaurus represents one of the largest abelisaurids.
facts.quote: The only known individual was about 7.5 - 8 m in length, making Carnotaurus one of the largest abelisaurids.

facts.statement: The left femur of the known specimen measures 103 cm in length but has an average diameter of only 11 cm.
facts.quote: The left femur (thigh bone) of the individual measures 103 cm in length, but shows an average diameter of only 11 cm.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the distinctive horns and muscular neck of Carnotaurus may have been used in intraspecific fighting.
facts.quote: The distinctive horns and the muscular neck may have been used in fighting others of its species.

facts.statement: Studies propose that rivaling Carnotaurus individuals may have fought using quick head blows, slow skull pushes, or head-on ramming with horns acting as shock absorbers.
facts.quote: According to separate studies, rivaling individuals may have combated each other with quick head blows, by slow pushes with the upper sides of their skulls, or by ramming each other head-on, using their horns as shock absorbers.

facts.statement: The diet of Carnotaurus is debated; some studies suggest it hunted large prey like sauropods, while others indicate it primarily ate smaller animals.
facts.quote: The feeding habits of Carnotaurus remain unclear: some studies suggested the animal was able to hunt down very large prey such as sauropods, while other studies found it preyed mainly on relatively small animals.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is a derived member of the Abelisauridae family, a group of large theropods that dominated predatory niches in southern Gondwana during the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus is a derived member of the Abelisauridae, a group of large theropods that occupied the large predatorial niche in the southern landmasses of Gondwana during the late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Within the Abelisauridae, Carnotaurus is often classified as a member of the Brachyrostra clade, which consists of short-snouted forms restricted to South America.
facts.quote: Within the Abelisauridae, the genus is often considered a member of the Brachyrostra, a clade of short-snouted forms restricted to South America.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had a skull measuring 59.6 cm in length that was proportionally shorter and deeper than any other large carnivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: The skull, measuring 59.6 cm in length, was proportionally shorter and deeper than in any other large carnivorous dinosaur.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus possessed a prominent pair of horns that protruded obliquely above its eyes.
facts.quote: A prominent pair of horns protruded obliquely above the eyes.

facts.statement: In 2020, Cerroni and colleagues agreed the horns supported keratinous sheaths but argued these sheaths were not much longer than the bony cores.
facts.quote: Mauricio Cerroni and colleagues, in 2020, agreed that the horns supported keratinous sheaths, but argued that these sheaths would not have been greatly longer than the bony cores.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had four premaxillary and twelve maxillary teeth on each side of the upper jaw and fifteen dentary teeth on each side of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: On each side of the upper jaws there were four premaxillary and twelve maxillary teeth, while the lower jaws were equipped with fifteen dentary teeth per side.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus's replacement teeth had low, flattened crowns that were closely spaced and inclined forward at approximately 45 degrees.
facts.quote: The replacement teeth had low, flattened crowns, were closely spaced, and inclined forwards at approximately 45°.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is the only known non-avian theropod dinosaur from which a basihyal bone has been found.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus is the only known non-avian theropod from which a basihyal is known.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had a neck that was nearly straight and unusually wide, especially at its base, unlike the S-curve seen in other theropods.
facts.quote: The neck was nearly straight, rather than having the S-curve seen in other theropods, and also unusually wide, especially towards its base.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus's forearm was only one-quarter the size of its upper arm.
facts.quote: The forearm was only a quarter the size of the upper arm.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus lacked carpalia in its hand, causing the metacarpals to articulate directly with the forearm.
facts.quote: There were no carpalia in the hand, so that the metacarpals articulated directly with the forearm.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is the first known theropod dinosaur to have a significant number of fossil skin impressions found on its skeleton.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus was the first theropod dinosaur discovered with a significant number of fossil skin impressions.

facts.statement: The skin of Carnotaurus consisted of a mosaic of polygonal, non-overlapping scales that were approximately 5 to 12 millimeters in diameter.
facts.quote: The skin was built up of a mosaic of polygonal, non-overlapping scales measuring approximately 5–12 mm in diameter.

facts.statement: There is no fossil evidence indicating that Carnotaurus had feathers.
facts.quote: There is no evidence of feathers.

facts.statement: Studies published in 2021 suggest that the larger feature scales on Carnotaurus were randomly distributed along the body rather than arranged in discrete rows as previously depicted.
facts.quote: More recent studies of the skin of Carnotaurus published in 2021 suggest that previous depictions of the scales on the body are inaccurate, and the larger feature scales were randomly distributed along the body, not distributed in discrete rows like in older artistic depictions and illustrations.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the variation in scale size on Carnotaurus may have helped regulate body heat through thermoregulation.
facts.quote: This scale differentiation may have been related to regulating body heat and shedding excess heat via thermoregulation due to its large body size and active lifestyle.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is a well-understood genus within the family Abelisauridae, which was restricted to the southern supercontinent Gondwana.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus is one of the best-understood genera of the Abelisauridae, a family of large theropods restricted to the ancient southern supercontinent Gondwana.

facts.statement: A 2024 study identified Carnotaurini as a valid clade containing Carnotaurus, Aucasaurus, Niebla, and Koleken.
facts.quote: A 2024 study recovered Carnotaurini as a valid clade consisting of Carnotaurus, Aucasaurus, Niebla and Koleken.

facts.statement: The function of Carnotaurus's horns is debated, with theories ranging from fighting conspecifics or killing prey to display for courtship or species recognition.
facts.quote: The use of these horns is not entirely clear. Several interpretations have revolved around use in fighting conspecifics or in killing prey, though a use in display for courtship or recognition of members of the same species is possible as well.

facts.statement: In 1998, researchers suggested Carnotaurus used its horns for ramming, calculating its neck muscles could withstand collisions at speeds of 5.7 meters per second.
facts.quote: Gerardo Mazzetta and colleagues (1998) suggested that Carnotaurus used its horns in a way similar to rams. They calculated that the neck musculature was strong enough to absorb the force of two individuals colliding with their heads frontally at a speed of 5.7 m/s each.

facts.statement: Fernando Novas suggested in 2009 that Carnotaurus's short skull and muscular neck were adaptations for delivering quick, strong head blows.
facts.quote: Fernando Novas (2009) interpreted several skeletal features as adaptations for delivering blows with the head. He suggested that the shortness of the skull might have made head movements quicker by reducing the moment of inertia, while the muscular neck would have allowed strong head blows.

facts.statement: Some studies propose that Carnotaurus rivals engaged in slow pushing matches rather than rapid headbutting.
facts.quote: Other studies suggest that rivaling Carnotaurus did not deliver rapid head blows, but pushed slowly against each other with the upper sides of their skulls.

facts.statement: In 2009, researchers argued that Carnotaurus's horns functioned to distribute compression forces to protect the brain during impacts.
facts.quote: Mazzetta and colleagues, in 2009, argued that the horns may have been a device for the distribution of compression forces without damage to the brain.

facts.statement: In 2018, Rafael Delcourt suggested Carnotaurus's horns were used for either slow shoving or striking the neck and flanks of opponents.
facts.quote: Rafael Delcourt, in 2018, suggested that the horns could have been used either in slow headbutting and shoving, as seen in the modern marine iguana, or in blows to the opponent's neck and flanks, as seen in the modern giraffe.

facts.statement: In 1998, researchers proposed that Carnotaurus might have used its horns to injure or kill small prey.
facts.quote: Gerardo Mazzetta and colleagues (1998) propose that the horns might also have been used to injure or kill small prey.

facts.statement: A 2009 study estimated the bite force of Carnotaurus at approximately 3,341 newtons.
facts.quote: In 2009, Mazzetta and colleagues estimated a bite force of around 3,341 newtons.

facts.statement: A 2022 study estimated the anterior bite force of Carnotaurus at around 3,392 newtons, slightly higher than a previous estimate.
facts.quote: A 2022 study estimating bite force for 33 different dinosaurs suggests that the bite force in Carnotaurus was around 3,392 newtons at the anterior portion of the jaws; slightly higher than the previous estimate.

facts.statement: François Therrien and colleagues (2005) questioned earlier interpretations, suggesting Carnotaurus had a bite force twice that of the American alligator.
facts.quote: This interpretation was questioned by François Therrien and colleagues (2005), who found that the biting force of Carnotaurus was twice that of the American alligator, which may have the strongest bite of any living tetrapod.

facts.statement: Analyses comparing Carnotaurus to modern Komodo dragons suggest its jaws were adapted for delivering slashing wounds to large prey rather than catching small prey with high precision.
facts.quote: These researchers also noted analogies with modern Komodo dragons: the flexural strength of the lower jaw decreases towards the tip linearly, indicating that the jaws were not suited for high precision catching of small prey but for delivering slashing wounds to weaken big prey.

facts.statement: Cerroni and colleagues (2020) debated the extent of skull flexibility, arguing that while the lower jaw was flexible, the skull itself had little to no kinesis due to a thickened roof and ossified joints.
facts.quote: Cerroni and colleagues, in 2020, argued that flexibility was restricted to the lower jaw, while the thickened skull roof and the ossification of several cranial joints suggest that the skull had no or only little kinesis.

facts.statement: Robert Bakker (1998) proposed that Carnotaurus primarily hunted very large prey, specifically sauropods.
facts.quote: Robert Bakker (1998) found that Carnotaurus mainly fed upon very large prey, especially sauropods.

facts.statement: Robert Bakker noted that Carnotaurus possessed skull adaptations like a short snout and strong occiput that had independently evolved in Allosaurus.
facts.quote: As he noted, several adaptations of the skull—the short snout, the relatively small teeth and the strong back of the skull (occiput)—had independently evolved in Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Calculations suggest the caudofemoralis muscle in Carnotaurus had a mass of 111 to 137 kg per leg.
facts.quote: The muscle mass was calculated at 111 to 137 kg per leg.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus likely had diminished ability to make tight turns because its stiff tail and hip had to move simultaneously.
facts.quote: As a consequence, the ability to make tight turns would have been diminished, because the hip and tail had to be turned simultaneously, unlike in other theropods.

facts.statement: CT scans revealed the endocranial cavity of Carnotaurus had a volume of 168.8 cm³.
facts.quote: The volume of the endocranial cavity was 168.8 cm3, although the brain would only have filled a fraction of this space.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated Carnotaurus brain size as either 50% or 37% of its endocranial cavity volume.
facts.quote: The authors used two different brain size estimates, assuming a brain size of 50% and 37% of the endocranial cavity, respectively.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had a reptile encephalization quotient larger than its relative Majungasaurus but smaller than that of tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: This results in a reptile encephalization quotient (a measure of intelligence) larger than that of the related Majungasaurus but smaller than in tyrannosaurids.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus possessed large olfactory bulbs and relatively small optic lobes, suggesting a keen sense of smell compared to sight.
facts.quote: The olfactory bulbs, which housed the sense of smell, were large, while the optic lobes, which were responsible for sight, were relatively small.

facts.statement: The estimated hearing range of Carnotaurus was below 3 kHz.
facts.quote: The hearing range was estimated to be below 3 kHz.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus fossils date to the Maastrichtian to lower Danian ages, approximately 69 to 64 million years ago.
facts.quote: Later, they were realized to pertain to the much younger La Colonia Formation, which, according to a 2021 study, dates to the Maastrichtian to lower Danian ages around 69–64 million years ago.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is known to be the latest South American abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus was the latest South American abelisaurid known.

facts.statement: Fossils of Carnotaurus were found in the La Colonia Formation, exposed on the southern slope of the North Patagonian Massif.
facts.quote: The La Colonia Formation is exposed over the southern slope of the North Patagonian Massif.

facts.statement: The environment where Carnotaurus lived likely consisted of estuaries, tidal flats, or coastal plains.
facts.quote: This part likely represents the deposits of an environment of estuaries, tidal flats or coastal plains.

facts.statement: The genus Carnotaurus was named by Bonaparte in 1985.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte, 1985

facts.statement: The species Carnotaurus sastrei was named by Bonaparte in 1985.
facts.quote: species_authority: Bonaparte, 1985

facts.statement: Carnotaurus sastrei is the only known species of the extinct genus Carnotaurus, a theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus sastrei (lat. "toro carnívoro de Anselmo Sastre"), o carnotauro en castellano, es la única especie conocida del género extinto Carnotaurus de dinosaurio terópodo de la familia Abelisauridae.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 69.9 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Vivió en el Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente entre 72 y 69,9 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is notable for having two small horns above its eyes, making it the first known carnivorous dinosaur with well-formed and defined horns.
facts.quote: Lo más notable de este dinosaurio son sus dos pequeños cuernos sobre los ojos en su pequeña cabeza, siendo el primer carnívoro que mostrara cuernos bien formados y definidos.

facts.statement: Fossil skin impressions of Carnotaurus revealed small osteoderms, or bony shields.
facts.quote: También se hallaron impresiones de la piel que presentaban pequeños osteodermos, escudos óseos.

facts.statement: The species name "sastrei" honors Anselmo Sastre, the owner of the estancia where the first and only specimen was found in Chubut, Argentina.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie "sastrei" le fue otorgado en honor a Anselmo Sastre, dueño de la estancia (Pocho Sastre) en el departamento de Telsen, provincia Chubut, Argentina, donde fue hallado el primer y único espécimen.

facts.statement: While Carnotaurus's diet is not fully clear, some studies of its skull morphology suggest it was capable of hunting large prey like sauropods.
facts.quote: Los hábitos alimentarios de Carnotaurus aún no están claros del todo para los investigadores, aunque algunos estudios de la morfología craneal sugieren que el animal era capaz de cazar presas muy grandes, como los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Other studies suggest Carnotaurus primarily fed on relatively small animals.
facts.quote: Otros estudios encontraron que se alimentaba principalmente de animales relativamente pequeños.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus was highly adapted for running and was possibly one of the fastest large theropods, reaching speeds of approximately 56 km/h.
facts.quote: Lo que sí se sabe es que Carnotaurus se adaptaba muy bien para correr y fue posiblemente uno de los terópodos más rápidos de gran tamaño, alcanzando aproximadamente una velocidad de 56 km/h a la hora de correr.

facts.statement: The most distinctive features of Carnotaurus are two thick horns above the eyes and extremely reduced, atrophied forelimbs with four fingers.
facts.quote: Las características más distintivas del Carnotaurus son dos cuernos gruesos sobre los ojos y unos miembros delanteros extremadamente reducidos y atrofiados, provistos de cuatro dedos.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus was the first theropod dinosaur discovered with complete fossil skin impressions.
facts.quote: Carnotaurus fue el primer dinosaurio terópodo descubierto con impresiones completas de piel fósil.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus skin was embedded with small osteoderms arranged in barrel-like columns parallel to the body's central axis.
facts.quote: La piel está incrustada por pequeños osteodermos, delineados en columnas de barriles paralelos al eje central del cuerpo.

facts.statement: Uniquely among theropods, Carnotaurus had osteoderms along the sides of its neck, back, and tail in irregular rows.
facts.quote: De manera única para los terópodos, tenía osteodermos, escudos óseos, a lo largo de los lados del cuello, la espalda y la cola en filas irregulares.

facts.statement: Stephen Czerkas suggests these osteoderms may have protected the animal's sides during fights with conspecifics or other theropods, noting similar structures in modern iguanas provide limited combat protection.
facts.quote: Stephen Czerkas sugiere que estas estructuras podrían proteger los lados del animal mientras luchaba contra miembros de su misma especie u otros terópodos, con el argumento de que las estructuras similares se pueden encontrar en el cuello de la moderna iguana, donde proporcionan una protección limitada en el combate.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had four fingers on each hand, a primitive trait compared to the Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: Sus extremidades anteriores eran más cortas en comparación con las del Tyrannosaurus, con cuatro dedos en cada mano, cosa considerada un rasgo primitivo entre los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus lacked a wrist bone, allowing its metacarpals to articulate directly with the forearm.
facts.quote: No había carpo en la mano, de modo que los metacarpianos articulaban directamente con el antebrazo.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the fourth finger, which was spur-like, was used to hold onto prey.
facts.quote: Se cree que este último era usado para sujetar a las presas.

facts.statement: Analysis by Mazzetta et al. suggests Carnotaurus was capable of rapid but not strong bites.
facts.quote: El análisis del diseño de la mandíbula de Carnotaurus por Mazzetta et al. sugiere que el animal era capaz de mordidas rápidas, pero no fuertes.

facts.statement: Researchers observed a high degree of skull flexibility in Carnotaurus, particularly in the lower jaw, similar to modern snakes.
facts.quote: Además, estos investigadores observaron un alto grado de flexibilidad del cráneo, especialmente en la mandíbula inferior, algo similar a las serpientes modernas.

facts.statement: Robert Bakker argued that Carnotaurus primarily fed on very large prey, especially sauropods.
facts.quote: Por otro lado, Robert Bakker encontró que el Carnotaurus se alimentaba principalmente de presas muy grandes, especialmente de saurópodos.

facts.statement: In 2020, Cerroni and colleagues argued that skull flexibility was restricted to the lower jaw, suggesting the rest of the skull had little to no movement.
facts.quote: Cerroni y sus colegas, en 2020, argumentaron que la flexibilidad estaba restringida a la mandíbula inferior, mientras que el techo del cráneo engrosado y la osificación de varias articulaciones craneales sugieren que el cráneo tenía poca o ninguna cinesis.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus belongs to the parent group Furileusauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Furileusauria

facts.statement: Carnotaurus is classified in the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: Carnotaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Carnotaurus had a safety factor of 92, suggesting its skull was over-engineered compared to the forces generated by its bite.
facts.quote: Existe una gran diferencia entre la máxima fuerza que resiste y la generada por una mordida. Esto le da un factor de seguridad de 92, que sugiere que el cráneo de Carnotaurus podría haber estado sobrediseñado.

facts.statement: The horns and strong fusion between frontal and parietal bones suggest the skull was designed to resist high compressive loads.
facts.quote: La presencia de cuernos y la fuerte fusión observada entre los huesos frontales y parietales sugieren que este sector del cráneo presenta un diseño para resistir elevadas cargas compresivas.

facts.statement: Carnotaurus likely used its jaw movement, tooth design, and neck muscles to cut and tear large food chunks to swallow without chewing.
facts.quote: El gran rango de movimientos y el apropiado diseño de sus dientes, conjuntamente con la fuerza originada por su musculatura del cráneo y del cuello, le habrían permitido a Carnotaurus cortar y desgarrar grandes trozos de alimento que tragaría sin masticar.
